idiom_name: extension functions on FlowContent (kotlinx.html DSL) or Thymeleaf utility objects under Spring
implementation_notes: There is no helper registry to plug into: kotlinx.html's type-safe builder makes a view helper an ordinary extension function on FlowContent (or on the view model), composed by calling it inside the markup DSL, and Kotlin's own documentation frames extension functions and properties as the way to add display helpers without touching the class. Under Spring Boot the same logic is written as extension functions on the view model plus Thymeleaf utility objects. The classic helper class is unnecessary; what still applies is the boundary rule - the function formats and emits, the controller or service retrieves. An object holding configuration shared across views (a locale bundle) is the justified remnant of the helper class.
pitfalls: Extension functions resolve statically: an overload chosen by the declared receiver type wins, and a member function with the same name always beats an extension - the helper can silently not be the one you wrote.
Extension properties cannot have backing fields, so per-render state in a helper forces an explicit field or map; keep helpers stateless instead.
The DSL writes to a writer or DOM directly, so escaping is the builder's responsibility - bypassing it with raw text puts XSS handling on the helper.
A helper declared on Any cannot use the surrounding markup receiver; declare it on FlowContent so it nests correctly inside other builders.
